newsitem.title: UK: UK B/socs net new approvals s/a 3.514 bln in Dec.
newsitem.headline: UK B/socs net new approvals s/a 3.514 bln in Dec.

text.p: The UK Building Societies Association (BSA) released the following data on lending (seasonally adjusted unless otherwise stated):
NOTES - approval = borrower accepts offer of advance; advance = actual loan, on average some 10 wks after commitment; advances tend to reflect new approvals made 2 or 3 mths ago.
The BSA said net lending rose by 48 percent in 1996 compared to 1995 and said the figures showed recovery strengthened as the year progressed.

It said net advances, at 13.244 billion stg, were the highest since 1992. "Other indicators also showed strong growth with mortgage approvals at their highest since 1989 and gross advances at their highest since 1991," the BSA said.
BSA Director-General Adrian Coles said the figures confirmed the housing market had hauled itself out of recession in 1996.
"It is likely that the recovery will continue in to 1997 but, crucially, without reaching the absurd heights of the boom in the late 1980s," he said.
"The scene is set for a strong, but sustainable, increase in lending, transactions and prices," Coles added.
The BSA said building societies had found conditions in the savings market easier when it became clear interest rates would fall no further and may rise modestly.

"With particularly attractive rates now becoming available on fixed rate and notice products, and equities beginning to look expensive, the upward trend in net receipts should continue into 1997," said Coles.
